Unlike methods that predict Gaussian parameters via feedforward networks conditioned on pose [S1], Gaussian Avatars optimizes the Gaussian ellipsoid parameters directly while enforcing geometric constraints, enabling high-fidelity rendering and relighting [S2, unofficial].

The claim states that Gaussian Avatars optimizes Gaussian ellipsoid parameters directly while enforcing geometric constraints, unlike methods that predict Gaussian parameters via feedforward networks conditioned on pose. However, Source [S1] explicitly states that 'Gaussian Avatar [47] ... leverages the SMPL model [48] as a prior to reconstruct full-body avatars using pose features to predict Gaussian parameters through a feedforward network.' This directly contradicts the claim that Gaussian Avatars does not use feedforward networks conditioned on pose to predict parameters. Additionally, Source [S1] describes the method associated with [S1] (which the claim contrasts against) as optimizing Gaussians constrained to triangles, but attributes the feedforward network approach to 'Gaussian Avatar' (likely referring to the paper cited as [47] in the text, which the claim calls 'Gaussian Avatars'). The claim misattributes the methodology.

This describes a specialized avatar reconstruction technique involving a parametric model (FLAME) and specific constraints, which differs from the general definition of 'standard' 3D Gaussian Splatting rasterization typically applied to unstructured point clouds or generic scenes. The position $\mathbf{p}_i$ is constrained to remain within the barycentric coordinates of triangle $t$ [S1][S3, unofficial].

The evidence explicitly states in both Source [S1] and Source [S3] that the method 'associates each triangle with a Gaussian that is optimized for the scene while being constrained to remain within its corresponding triangle.' The claim states that the position is constrained to remain within the barycentric coordinates of the triangle. In the context of 3D geometry and computer graphics, constraining a point (or Gaussian center) to remain 'within its corresponding triangle' is mathematically equivalent to constraining it within the triangle's barycentric coordinate space (where barycentric coordinates are non-negative and sum to 1). Therefore, the evidence supports the claim.
